 Hasan’s unique day: Record five-for, rare stumping and five-country milestone
 Published : 6 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 6 November 2026, 13:21
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter from Sylhet 
 Photo: Firoz Ahmed 
 Hasan Mahmud became the record-holder for the most five-wicket hauls by a Bangladesh pacer in Test cricket. On the second day of the Sylhet Test against West Indies today, he overtook Shahadat Hossain’s tally of four Test five-wicket hauls. 
 Hasan had the new ball with West Indies in the driving seat, but he quickly turned things around with the wickets of Amir Jangoo and Windies skipper Roston Chase off back-to-back deliveries. 
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 He had picked up a hat-trick in the UAE in the one-off Test against Afghanistan and came close to a second when the umpire adjudged Joshua Bishop lbw off the hattrick delivery of the 82nd over. 
 Read more Hasan's career-best figures of 6 for 90 helps bowl out West Indies for 356 
 "]
However, Bishop reviewed, and replays showed an inside edge onto the pads. Not to be thwarted, Hasan and Litton Das combined for an extraordinary dismissal as Hasan clinched his five-wicket haul with the wicket of Bishop. Standing up to the stumps to Hasan, Litton effected a brilliant stumping, waiting just long enough for Bishop to lift his feet. 
With that dismissal, Hasan also became the first Bangladesh pacer to claim a stumping off his bowling.
 Hasan’s five-wicket haul also saw him become just the second bowler, after Australia spinner Nathan Lyon, to take five wickets in an innings in five different countries. 
 Read more Spin plans flop as Taskin seeks the ‘extraordinary’ on Day 2 of Sylhet Test 
He had previously taken all his five-wicket hauls away from home. He has bagged five-wicket hauls in Rawalpindi, Chennai, Darwin, Abu Dhabi and now Sylhet. 
 Five-wicket hauls by Bangladesh pacers in Test cricket 
 Hasan Mahmud – 5 (19 Tests)
 Shahadat Hossain – 4 (38 Tests)
 Nahid Rana – 2 (12 Tests)
 Robiul Islam – 2 (9 Tests)
 Manjurul Islam, Rubel Hossain, Ebadot Hossain, Syed Khaled Ahmed, Taskin Ahmed and Shoriful Islam – 1 each
